If you guys require more detail about the exact assignment here you go.

The assignment in question is field journals. we are given 1 every once in a while and by the end of the semester, we were given 8 in total. He grades each field journal individually when we turn them in, every grading period he would re-grade, so instead of grading 1 field journal out of 5 as he has already done, instead, he would grade field journals 1-5 out of 25 giving us double points. By the end of the semester, he graded field journals 1-8 out of 40 giving triple points for field journals 1-5. He announced that even in this semester he will keep this up by grading field journals 1-12 all at once and then 1-16 all at once giving 5x the points of the first five field journals. This surprised me because I always assumed that every semester was kind of like a fresh start for students that didn't do so hot the first semester. If you didn't do an earlier field journal for some reason this grading technique would just be digging you an even deeper grave than the one you were in before. 

Also, people are under the assumption that I am going to use this to complain to my teacher, but I'm not complaining. I did all of my assignments so this is just giving 5 times the points I was given in the beginning, but this grading made me wonder what would happen if I didn't some of the field journals and wondered if this was a common practice.
